title: Jumping into January: 8 Tips to Reclaim Your Routine After the Holidays
excerpt: JUMP INTO JANUARY! 🎉🎈 I hope you had a fun holiday break. I certainly did. We spent the entire holiday here in Austin, allowing plenty of time to rest...
content: JUMP INTO JANUARY! 🎉🎈
I hope you had a fun holiday break. I certainly did. We spent the entire holiday here in Austin, allowing plenty of time to truly relax.
Don't laugh, but one day I watched six Hallmark-type movies, all while lying on the sofa, head resting on a fluffy pillow, munching freshly popped, buttery popcorn. Heaven! 😊
We also met up with friends at some great parties and open houses. Just enough of them to break up our days and the evening parties gave us an excuse to sleep in late the next morning.

Of course, Beth and I live states away from each other, but I can report she also enjoyed her holiday break. She has the added pleasure of celebrating her birthday just days after the first of the year when most of us are still on break. When I asked her how her holiday and birthday were, she answered enthusiastically, “Fabulous!!” She had a chance to relax and she spent all her special days with good friends and her grown kids. Ah, yes, the holidays were wonderful.

And now we're back to work. We're back to schedules. We're making resolutions, filling up calendars. We're getting calls from unrecognized numbers. We're scheduling annual appointments. We have a “to-do” list again. And if you're anything like me, the routines and habits you adhered to so very effortlessly before the holidays now feel like somebody else's schedule.
Here are our 8 tips to gently step back into our rhythm:

1. START SMALL: Don't overwhelm yourself thinking you need to execute the perfect high dive into the new year. Jump into the shallow end and get used to the water.
  2. START WITH YOUR 'HAPPY HABITS': We value all of our habits, but some are more fun than others. Start with your most enjoyable habits like gratitude journaling.
  3. PLAN YOUR DAYS: It might be helpful as you ease into the new year to plan at least part of your day.
  4. PRIORITIZE SLEEP: Going back to our regular sleeping pattern seems to help restore energy quickly.
  5. EMBRACE THE POWER OF MORNING LIGHT: Simply spending a few minutes outside in the morning resets your circadian rhythm and boosts your mood.
  6. TACKLE CHRISTMAS CLUTTER: Consider packing away the holiday decorations. It is difficult to think clearly when surrounded by clutter.
  7. COOKIE CLUTTER: Return to simple, nutritious meals that provide steady all-day fuel.
  8. PROGRESS OVER PERFECTION: Accept that it takes time to get fully back on track. Practice self-compassion.
HAPPY 2025! Let's greet the New Year with expectation and optimism. Practice self-compassion, hang around good people, and live fully every day.

title: Holiday Gift List for your Besties over 60
excerpt: I don't know about you, but boy, this month is truly getting away from me! To be perfectly honest I've not started any Christmas shopping...
content: I don't know about you, but boy, this month is truly getting away from me! To be perfectly honest I've not started any Christmas shopping. To be really honest, I don't even have a list yet!
After all, who would we be without our girlfriends!? If you're feeling a little behind and could use not only a word of encouragement but a list of gift ideas, this is the post for you.

• Reading Glasses: Mid-range magnification readers with fashionable frames for the friend who misplaces hers.
  • Pill Holder Key Chain: Keep mid-day essentials handy on the road without carrying bottles.
  • eLearning: Platforms like Masterclass or online courses for curious, lifelong learners.
  • Insulated Car Cups: High-end travel tumblers that keep tea or coffee warm for hours.
  • The Gift of Shared Time: An afternoon museum outing or uninterrupted lunch date.
At this stage in our lives, what matters most is the genuine love and friendship behind the gesture.

title: When Christmas Doesn't Feel Like Christmas: Nine Tips to Put the Happy Back
excerpt: Feeling a bit 'Bah Humbug' this holiday season? We totally understand. The holidays can bring unexpected pressure, loneliness, or grief...
content: Feeling a bit 'Bah Humbug' this holiday season? We totally understand. The holidays can bring unexpected pressure, loneliness, or memories that make celebration feel complicated rather than joyful.
Here are nine gentle ways to reclaim your peace and joy:

1. Acknowledge Your True Feelings: You don't have to force cheerfulness. Be honest about where your heart is.
  2. Scale Back Expectations: A single candle and a wreath can bring plenty of festive spirit without exhaustion.
  3. Create a New Tradition: Start a fresh, quiet custom that doesn't carry heavy baggage from the past.
  4. Reach Out to Someone in Need: Volunteering or sending a supportive note dissolves loneliness quickly.
  5. Step Outside Daily: Crisp winter air and daylight reset our outlook.
  6. Listen to Comforting Music: Swap frantic radio tunes for soothing acoustic tracks.
  7. Say 'No' Without Guilt: Protect your rest and decline overwhelming invitations.
  8. Indulge in Small Luxuries: Fresh bed linens, warm herbal teas, and good books.
  9. Focus on Gratitude: Name three things you are thankful for every evening.

title: Thanksgiving 2024: Navigating the Holiday in an Election Year
excerpt: Wow! What a year! As the old saying goes, 'Unless you've been living under a rock,' I think we can all agree this has been another whirlwind season...
content: Wow! What a year! As the old saying goes, 'Unless you've been living under a rock,' I think we can all agree this has been another whirlwind season of news, opinions, and spirited discussions across every corner of the country.
Gathering around the family table during an election year can test anyone's patience. But as women with years of perspective, we have the unique power to set the emotional tone in our homes:
'Peace is not the absence of disagreement, but the presence of grace and mutual respect.'

Before welcoming guests, agree on a simple mindset rule: keep gratitude at center stage. Steer conversations toward family memories, recipes, and what connects us rather than what divides us. Guard your peace of mind and make love the centerpiece of your holiday table.

title: The Power of Living in the Present Moment
excerpt: There is a bible verse that most of us are aware of but few of us truly follow (including me.) The Bible verse says, 'Tomorrow is not promised'...
content: There is a bible verse that most of us are aware of but few of us truly follow (including me.) The Bible verse says, 'Tomorrow is not promised.' How often do we let worry over tomorrow rob us of the sweetness right in front of our eyes today?

Mind management and spiritual peace in our sixties require deliberately practicing presence. When you sip your morning tea, taste it. When you listen to your friend laugh on the telephone, absorb it without checking your clock. Yesterday is gone and tomorrow hasn't arrived; all we are ever handed is this sacred current moment.
Give yourself permission today to put down yesterday's regrets and tomorrow's checklist. Breathe in, look around, and enjoy the right now.

title: Avoiding the mental pitfalls of Autumn: In Six Steps
excerpt: Each season has its separate and unique personality. Ready or not Winter confidently marches into our lives with dramatic weather shifts...
content: Each season has its separate and unique personality. Ready or not Winter confidently marches into our lives with dramatic weather shifts, shorter daylight hours, and cooler winds that naturally tempt us to isolate.
To avoid slipping into seasonal gloom or mental ruts, here are six practical steps to stay vibrant and energized throughout the fall:

1. Catch the Morning Light: Step outside within an hour of waking to balance your circadian rhythm.
  2. Warm Your Nourishment: Transition to grounding, warm meals—roasted root vegetables, slow-cooked stews, and herbal broths.
  3. Prioritize Social Connection: Don't let cold evenings keep you secluded; arrange regular coffee dates.
  4. Establish an Indoor Project: Reorganize photo books, paint, or start a new reading series.
  5. Practice Daily Gratitude Journaling: Write down three blessings every evening.
  6. Stay Physically Active: Keep joints mobile with indoor yoga and gentle stretching.

title: Hydration, Wholesome Eating, and Fueling Your Sixties
excerpt: What we put into our bodies directly impacts how clearly we think. Why simple water intake and unrefined staples become our greatest superpower...
content: As mature women, our hydration reflex naturally diminishes, meaning we often don't register thirst until our energy levels have already dipped. Nutrition past sixty isn't about restrictive diets—it's about fueling mental clarity, gut health, and radiant vitality.
Our core food & hydration pillars:

• The Morning Water Ritual: Drink 16 ounces of warm water with lemon before morning coffee.
  • Color on Every Plate: Deep leafy greens, fresh berries, and antioxidant-rich root vegetables.
  • Mindful Savoring: Eating unhurriedly away from screens.
  • Electrolytes & Herbal Infusions: Maintaining steady cellular hydration with minerals and natural teas.

title: Guarding Your Sleep: Conquering Restlessness Past Sixty
excerpt: Sleep patterns evolve as we grow older, but deep restorative rest is non-negotiable. Here are our essential evening wind-down rituals...
content: Hormonal shifts, racing thoughts, or changes in daily circadian cues often make continuous eight-hour sleep elusive in our sixties. Yet restful sleep is the very foundation upon which all emotional resilience sits.
Here is our sanctuary checklist for restorative sleep:

1. Digital Sunset at 8:30 PM: Trade blue-light phone scrolling for paper books or audiobooks.
  2. A Cool, Dark Bedroom: Keep bedroom temperatures between 65-68°F.
  3. Magnesium & Chamomile: A warm evening infusion to naturally relax muscular tension.
  4. The 'Brain Dump' Pad: Write tomorrow's checklist on paper so your brain can turn off.

title: To Dye or Not to Dye: The Gray Hair Conversation
excerpt: Few decisions spark more conversation among mature women than embracing silver strands or keeping our salon appointments...
content: Few topics bring out more passion, hesitation, and humor among women over sixty than what to do with our hair! Do we embrace the natural silver crown we earned, or do we continue visiting our beloved salon colorists?
Beth and I have had this conversation many times over coffee. The truth is: mind management means choosing what brings you confidence without bowing to anyone else's expectations.

If you love your rich color and salon days, own it with joy. If you decide to transition to natural gray or silver, rock it with total pride. The beauty of this season of life is that the choice belongs entirely to you.

title: Movement as Medicine: Gentle Daily Habits for Lifelong Agility
excerpt: You don't need high-impact aerobics to stay agile and vibrant. Here is how gentle movement preserves our balance and stamina...
content: In our twenties and thirties, exercise was often framed around intensity and burning calories. Past sixty, movement transforms into something far more valuable: freedom, joint mobility, balance, and independence.
Our favorite daily practices:

• Gentle Morning Stretching: Awakening the spine and hips before sitting down.
  • Brisk Neighborhood Walks: 20 to 30 minutes in daylight to strengthen the heart and clear mental chatter.
  • Balance Training: Practicing standing on one foot near the kitchen counter while brewing tea.
  • Light Resistance: Keeping bands or light weights handy to preserve bone density and muscle tone.

title: Cultivating Sacred Friendships in Our Sixties
excerpt: Making and keeping authentic friends as mature adults takes intention. Why close girlfriends are vital to emotional well-being...
content: Research consistently shows that meaningful relationships are the single greatest predictor of longevity and mental acuity as we age. But sustaining friendships across busy family schedules, health changes, and geographic moves takes intention.
Here is what Beth and I have discovered about friendship past sixty:
'A true friend allows you to show up as you are—without makeup, pretense, or explanation.'
Invest in the friends who celebrate your victories, listen without judging, and make you laugh until your stomach hurts. Pick up the phone today and tell someone what they mean to you.

title: Finding Daily Joy in the Simple Things
excerpt: Joy doesn't require grand vacations or monumental milestones. It lives right here in our everyday routines...
content: Too often we postpone happiness for the next trip, the next celebration, or the next milestone. But maturity teaches us that the sweetest joy lives right in the ordinary moments of everyday life.

The warm aroma of morning coffee. The sound of birds outside your bedroom window. A handwritten note from a child or grandchild. A funny story shared over the phone. When we train our minds to notice and savor these micro-moments, life becomes extraordinarily rich.
